articles.title: From ‘Star Wars’ to ‘Alien: How Val Kilmer, Gene Wilder and 3 other late Hollywood stars returned to the screen through AI, CGI and digital effects
articles.summary: Explore how Hollywood is using AI, CGI, and digital effects to resurrect the likenesses of late stars like Val Kilmer and Gene Wilder for modern films. Delve into the ethical debates surrounding consent and the rights of deceased actors as their legacies continue on screen.
articles.body: The use of artificial intelligence (AI), computer-generated imagery (CGI) and digital visual effects has made it possible for filmmakers to bring the likenesses of late actors back to the screen. While some productions have relied on previously unseen footage and digital enhancements, others have recreated an actor’s appearance or voice using advanced technology. These techniques have also sparked debate in Hollywood over consent, creative ethics and the rights of actors after their deaths. From Carrie Fisher’s appearances in the Star Wars franchise to Val Kilmer’s AI-generated role in As Deep as the Grave, here are five late Hollywood stars whose screen legacies have continued through digital recreations.Carrie Fisher in ‘Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker’ and ‘Rogue One: A Star Wars Story’Carrie Fisher, best known for playing Princess Leia in the 'Star Wars' franchise, appeared in films released after her death on December 27, 2016, at the age of 60. For 'Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker' (2019), filmmaker J. J. Abrams used previously unreleased footage of Fisher shot for 'Star Wars: The Force Awakens'. The material was incorporated into the film with the help of visual effects, allowing Fisher’s Leia to remain part of the story. Her daughter, Billie Lourd, also served as a body double for some scenes.According to Industrial Light & Magic (ILM) and The Guardian, Fisher had also appeared digitally in 'Rogue One: A Star Wars Story' (2016), released shortly before her death. Since the film takes place before the events of the original 'Star Wars', the visual effects team recreated a younger version of Leia. Norwegian actor Ingvild Deila served as the on-screen stand-in, with digital effects used to reproduce Fisher’s appearance. The sequence relied on CGI and archival material rather than modern generative AI. The work was part of ILM’s effort to recreate the character’s appearance from the original film.Val Kilmer in ‘As Deep as the Grave’Val Kilmer, who died on April 1, 2025, at the age of 65, is set to appear in 'As Deep as the Grave' through an AI-generated performance. The actor had been cast as Father Fintan, a Catholic priest and Native American spiritualist, but his declining health prevented him from travelling to the set and filming his scenes. According to Variety, writer-director Coerte Voorhees received the cooperation of Kilmer’s estate and his daughter, Mercedes Kilmer, to recreate the actor for the film. The production used photographs from different stages of his life, archival footage and voice material to create the performance.Explaining why he wanted Kilmer for the role, Voorhees told Variety, “He was the actor I wanted to play this role. It was very much designed around him.” He added that the part drew on Kilmer’s Native American heritage and his connection to the American Southwest. The decision has drawn scrutiny amid Hollywood’s wider debate over AI-generated performances. However, Kilmer’s family has supported the project, with his daughter saying that her father viewed emerging technologies as a way to expand storytelling possibilities. The film’s use of AI has brought renewed attention to questions surrounding consent, compensation and the use of an actor’s likeness after death.Peter Cushing in ‘Rogue One: A Star Wars Story’British actor Peter Cushing, who died on August 11, 1994, at the age of 81, returned to the 'Star Wars' universe in 'Rogue One: A Star Wars Story' (2016). Cushing had played Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin in 'Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope' (1977), and the character was brought back for the prequel. Actor Guy Henry performed the role on set, while the visual effects team at Industrial Light & Magic digitally recreated Cushing’s face and likeness. The process combined Henry’s performance with CGI and reference material from Cushing’s earlier work. The filmmakers obtained permission from Cushing’s estate to use his likeness, according to The Guardian.The recreation became a prominent talking point after the film’s release, raising questions about the ethics of digitally reproducing actors who are no longer alive. The visual effects supervisor, John Knoll, defended the decision, telling The Guardian that the work had been done with care and in consultation with the actor’s estate. Cushing’s appearance in Rogue One remains one of Hollywood’s best-known examples of a deceased performer being digitally recreated for a major studio film.Gene Wilder in ‘Wonka’s The Golden Ticket’Gene Wilder, who played Willy Wonka in the 1971 film 'Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory,' returned to the character’s world through his AI-recreated voice in Netflix’s reality competition series 'Wonka’s The Golden Ticket', released in 2026. Wilder died on August 29, 2016, at the age of 83. Rather than recreating his physical appearance, the production used AI technology to reproduce his distinctive voice for the series. According to Netflix’s Tudum, the team sought permission from Wilder’s widow, Karen Boyer, who provided access to old recordings and audiobooks to help recreate his humour, tone and vocal mannerisms.Showrunner Alison Holloway explained why Wilder was the team’s choice, saying, “The only person that could be Wonka is Gene Wilder.” She also expressed gratitude for his widow’s approval of the project. The use of Wilder’s voice offers a different example of posthumous digital recreation, with AI being used for audio rather than a visual performance. It has also added to the ongoing discussion about how a late performer’s voice and identity should be used in new productions.Ian Holm in ‘Alien: Romulus’Ian Holm, the British actor remembered by many audiences as Bilbo Baggins in 'The Lord of the Rings' trilogy, appeared posthumously in 'Alien: Romulus' (2024). Holm died on June 19, 2020, at the age of 88. In the science-fiction film, his likeness was used for Rook, an android resembling Ash, the character he played in the original 'Alien' (1979). Director Fede Álvarez and the visual effects team combined practical effects, CGI and AI-assisted techniques to recreate Holm’s likeness. Actor Daniel Betts contributed to the physical performance, while the production secured permission from Holm’s family and estate.Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter, Álvarez explained the decision to bring back Holm’s likeness, saying, “It was unfair that the likeness of Ash was never used again.” He added that the team proceeded with the approval of Holm’s widow and children. The recreation proved controversial among some viewers, with criticism directed at both the decision to use a deceased actor’s likeness and the visual effects. The film’s release renewed debate about the boundaries between visual effects, AI and the rights of performers whose images continue to appear on screen after their deaths.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Kristen Bell says she cries weekly over challenges of family life: ‘It’s brutal’
articles.summary: “Do not think because I am on your television that it is easy for me,” the actress said in a new interview.
articles.body:
Kristen Bell admits she regularly cries over the challenges of family life.

"Do not think because I am on your television that it is easy for me," the actress said in a new interview.

Bell shares two daughters — Lincoln, 13, and Delta, 11 — with husband and fellow actor Dax Shepard.

Just because Kristen Bell is smiling on the red carpet doesn't mean her personal life is always sunshine and rainbows.

The Nobody Wants This star continued her candid streak while discussing the challenges of marriage and raising two kids in the public eye during a recent interview.

"It's hard. Do not think because I am on your television that it is easy for me," Bell bluntly told Bustle . "It's brutal. I cry weekly."

Bell shares two daughters with her husband of 13 years, Dax Shepard , and is no stranger to speaking honestly about the rocky times that the couple have endured. During the interview, she noted that it feels especially important to open up about those difficulties as a public figure, so other people see their own struggles reflected back at them.

"Oftentimes when you're in that cyclone of puberty, you could think, My kid is the only one doing this," Bell pointed out. "And that is just simply not a fact."

For his part, Shepard praised his wife for her strength in their relationship, sharing that he knew early on that she would be "a force of nature to be reckoned with." He said that he has since been proven correct, joking, "She's not afraid of the gorilla she lives with."

Bell and Shepard have been together since 2007. The couple tied the knot in 2013 after waiting for California to pass same-sex marriage into law, in solidarity with LGBTQ couples who had previously been denied the right to marry. The actors are parents to daughters Lincoln, 13, and Delta, 11.

Bell noted that when it comes to booking future gigs, she takes care to put her family first.

"Is this going to pull me away from my kids too much? Will I still be able to be the mom that I want to be? That's really the No. 1, to be honest. There's nothing higher than that," she said. "I would easily let my whole career and all its legacy and notoriety 'disapparate' tomorrow if it meant sacrificing something major in my kids' lives, or not being there."

As for the struggles Bell and Shepard have endured, the couple regularly open up about their past in interviews and on Shepard's Armchair Expert podcast. They have spoken about issues including their brief breakup , which came shortly before they were engaged, and reacting to one another performing intimate scenes with other actors.

Last October, the couple faced backlash for a controversial anniversary post in which Bell recounted Shepard saying to her, "I would never kill you. A lot of men have killed their wives at a certain point. Even though I'm heavily incentivized to kill you, I never would."

The post was met with ire from social media users who labeled the post "tone deaf" and "insensitive" toward victims of domestic violence. Reacting to the pushback just days later, Bell affirmed her deep commitment to her partner of nearly 20 years: "Sometimes it's gonna ebb and sometimes it's gonna flow, but we're not gonna have checks and balances because we're gonna realize it's not me against you, it's us against the world."

articles.title: Blake Shelton 'sick and stunned' as he mourns heartbreaking death – Gwen Stefani reacts
articles.summary: Blake Shelton shared an emotional tribute to John Anderson, revealing he told the country legend he loved him just days before his death. See details
articles.body:
Blake Shelton is "sick" and "stunned." The Grammy-winning singer opened up about his heartbreak on Thursday, October 22 after losing his friend and fellow country singer, JohnAnderson .

The "Boys 'Round Here" singer shared what he is grateful to have said to John during their final meeting, just three days before the country music legend's death.

Following the news that John had died on Wednesday, October 21, aged 71, Blake posted a photograph of them smiling together and reflected on losing both a musical hero and a friend.

"There is too much for me to say about @johnanderson in just a statement. I am sick and I am stunned. But I am a very lucky man," he wrote.

"I got the opportunity to find out that my hero wasn't just the guy I hoped he'd be. He was so much more than that. John was my friend."

The pair had seen each other at the Country Music Hall of Fame's Medallion Ceremony in Nashville on Sunday, October 18. Blake had no idea it would be their last encounter.

"I got to see him last Sunday and I don't even know why but I told him I loved him. That is what fills my heart in this moment," he continued. "My love and prayers go out to John's family. This one really hurts."

Blake's wife and fellow singer Gwen Stefani , 57, reacted to her husband's heartbreak, writing on his post: "Thank you for introducing our family to such a Legend -a one-of-a-kind voice. He will always be part the soundtrack of music that defines who our family. we love u John."

Tim McGraw remembers final evening with John Anderson

Blake was not the only singer remembering a conversation with John at Sunday's ceremony. Tim McGraw , who was among the artists being inducted that evening, also shared a photograph with the country star and recalled the pleasure of spending time together.

"We talked, we laughed, we sang his songs that I loved so much together, just goofing off," Tim wrote on Instagram.

Reba McEntire also joined the tributes, reflecting the affection for John across generations of performers. His distinctive voice had made songs including "Swingin'," "Straight Tequila Night" and "Seminole Wind" enduring country favorites.

John Anderson's family announces his death at 71

John's family said he died peacefully in his sleep. No cause of death has been announced. He is survived by his wife, Jamie , daughters Alexa and Brionna , and their families.

His career began far from the honors he would eventually receive. After leaving Florida for Nashville in 1972, John took construction work while pursuing his musical ambitions.

One of those jobs involved helping build the Grand Ole Opry House, where he worked on the roof before eventually realizing his dream of performing on its stage.

He went on to release more than 20 albums and was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024.

For his family, however, the announcement of his death focused on the man they knew away from the stage. "He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely and made every ordinary moment feel special."

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s sister Stella Parton claims she received death threats and hate mail after raising Tennessee voting machine concerns, says ‘she would be concerned about me today’; denies being paid by Democrats
articles.summary: Dolly Parton’s sister Stella Parton has claimed she is receiving hate mail and death threats after speaking out about an alleged voting machine issue in
articles.body: Dolly Parton’s sister Stella Parton has claimed she is receiving hate mail and death threats after speaking out about an alleged voting machine issue in Tennessee, adding that her late sister’s “heart was broken” over the political situation in the United States.Stella, who has been outspoken about her political views on social media, said the backlash would not stop her from raising concerns about human rights and the country’s future. She also claimed that she had faced hostile messages and death threats for years because of her criticism of Donald Trump.“I’ve been getting hate mail and death threats and nasty comments since I started posting on Trump ten years ago,” Stella wrote on Facebook. “I’ve been a human rights activist for decades and that will never change.”In another post, she reflected on her late sister’s concerns about her activism and recalled how Dolly had supported her despite their different approaches to public life.“My big sister’s heart was broken over it but she respected my work. We just worked differently,” Stella wrote. “She would be concerned about me today, when my life was threatened, just like she used to be concerned when I raced cars in celebrity races.”Stella Parton alleges voting machine repeatedly selected Marsha BlackburnThe controversy began after Stella, 77, claimed that a voting machine at the Hermitage branch of the Nashville Public Library repeatedly selected Republican gubernatorial candidate Marsha Blackburn when she tried to cast her ballot for someone else.In a Facebook post on Wednesday, Stella said she had voted during early voting in Nashville the previous week and had to correct her selection three times.“In Tennessee last week at the Hermitage Library where I voted, I had to go back three times and correct my vote because it kept defaulting to Marsha Blackburn,” she wrote. “I would never vote for her for anything.”Stella did not disclose which candidate she intended to vote for. Jerri Green is the Democratic candidate in Tennessee’s gubernatorial race, alongside independent candidates.Urging voters to check their selections carefully, Stella added, “I’m putting this out here because when we vote, we take it seriously but we try not to hold up the long lines. Do it anyway. Don’t let them rig this election.”She later said she was “frightened and frustrated” by the alleged incident and expressed anger over what she described as a lack of accountability in American politics.Stella denies being paid by Democrats to speak about voting machinesAs her posts attracted attention, Stella said some people had accused the Democratic Party of paying her to make claims about the voting equipment. She rejected the allegation, insisting that neither party had ever paid or offered her money.“I have never received or been offered one dime from either party ever,” she wrote. “Everything I post and all the work I do for my state and country is for human rights not any political party.”Stella also criticised political polarisation and said her activism was driven by her commitment to human rights rather than party loyalty. In another post, she expressed hope that Americans would eventually be able to have respectful conversations about the safety and wellbeing of children.She also raised concerns about possible interference by Elon Musk and Russian online accounts. However, there is no credible evidence establishing that Musk or Russian accounts tampered with Tennessee’s election operations.Tennessee election officials respond to voting machine allegationsTennessee election officials have disputed the suggestion that the reported incidents demonstrate deliberate vote manipulation.In a statement to The Tennessean, officials said: “Tennessee’s voting systems are designed with multiple safeguards to help ensure that ballots are recorded consistent with voter intent.”Tennessee Elections Coordinator Mark Goins told WSMV that the reported problems were “not a vote-flipping situation”. He suggested that unintended touches on touchscreen machines could explain some of the issues reported by voters.Chad Gray, election administrator in Williamson County, said officials there had found no discrepancies in their voting equipment. He added that if concerns arose, representatives from each party could examine the devices to ensure they were functioning properly.Other voters claim they experienced similar problemsStella’s Facebook post drew comments from other users who said they had encountered similar touchscreen issues at polling stations.One commenter claimed to have experienced the problem at the Holt Library in Brentwood, adding that they caught the incorrect selection before submitting their ballot.Another said they had to ensure the machine registered their intended choice of Jerri Green before printing the ballot. A third person, who said they had voted at the Hermitage Library, claimed they had to press the button for Green three times before the selection registered.These accounts have not independently established that votes were deliberately changed or that the reported incidents were part of a coordinated effort to influence the election.Dolly Parton kept her political views privateStella’s outspoken political activism contrasts with the public approach of her elder sister, Dolly Parton, who was famously private about her voting preferences and did not publicly disclose which candidates she supported.Dolly, the celebrated country singer-songwriter and philanthropist, died aged 80 on August 25, 2026, following a battle with cancer. She was admired by fans across the political spectrum, while Stella has frequently used social media to speak about human rights and criticise political figures.Stella has maintained that the criticism and threats will not silence her, saying she intends to continue speaking out on issues she believes affect the country and its people.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Former Gosselin Family Housekeeper and Nanny Claims She Saw Kate Abuse Collin and Reported It (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Collin made several claims against his mom in his new memoir, ‘In the Shadow of Eight’
articles.body:
A former house cleaner and part-time nanny for the Gosselin family is speaking out to PEOPLE

The former employee, who worked for the family for six months, alleges strict household rules left the children unable to play freely at home

Now a mother of twins, she hopes her account validates Collin Gosselin's experiences

While Ashley H. was studying for her master's degree in social work in her 20s in 2013, she'd watch TLC's Kate Plus 8 and dream of having a big family of kids someday like matriarch Kate Gosselin's .

Through the years, Kate had given her hope — as she, like Kate, struggled with years of infertility.

"I used to watch the show, like, 'My gosh, this is actually real. You can have infertility issues and you can still have kids,'" Ashley, who prefers to not reveal her last name, recalls to PEOPLE.

At the time, Ashley, now 42, was also working as a nanny. She came across an online posting for a nannying job one day and was surprised to learn it was for Kate and her eight children: twins Mady and Cara and sextuplets Collin, Alexis, Joel, Leah, Aaden and Hannah.

"She didn't say who she was [in the post], just that the nanny could live on the estate, and you could tell she was very, very wealthy," she says. "So, I met her at Starbucks, and she showed up in her sports car."

During their meeting, Ashley realized her class schedule would conflict with the schedule Kate needed a nanny for, so she took a job as her house cleaner and fill-in nanny instead.

When she got to Kate's home in Wernersville, Pa., which was only about 20 minutes from where she studied at Alvernia University, she remembers the "big beautiful family pictures" hanging on the wall.

"I used to think, like, 'Oh, I can't wait to have this someday,'" she says. "Now, I have my nice little house, and I have my canvas pictures of my family up on my walls. But I promised my house would never look unlived-in like Kate's."

Ashley claims that the reality in Kate's home was much different than what was portrayed on TV. She decided to speak out now to back the claims of physical and emotional abuse Collin made against his mom in his memoir, In The Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood .

"She very much outwardly treated Collin different," Ashley says. "She 110 percent abused Collin. It's hard to almost put into words the specific hate that she had towards Collin. You could just feel it. I saw her grab Collin many, many times."

Ashley says Kate had a "house manual" of rules for staff, which included not being able to take pictures of the kids and keeping the family dog out of the house, except for the basement.

"The house was to look unlived-in at all times," she says. "She would have weekly chores, biweekly chores, and they would include having a toothpick and going around the edges of the fridge."

"She wouldn't let the kids do anything," she continues. "There was never toys out. There was never things out. They couldn't live."

Ashley claims the kids were only allowed "either one or two school outfits per week because it would cause too much laundry" and that the interactions between Kate and the kids were "robotic."

"It was not loving," she says. "She very much made it known who was a favorite, who wasn't, who's annoying. Someone would come and pick the dog up for grooming, but she treated her kids basically worse than animals."

One day, Ashley says she opened up a drawer of school supplies and was surprised to find a big, red plastic spoon in it as "everything in the house was always so meticulous."

She asked the kids why the spoon was in there, and "instantly, I'm pretty sure it was Alexis who said, 'Oh, that's the spoon mommy uses when she gets mad.'"

That pushed Ashley to leave the job after only six months.

"I was like, "Oh, okay. I can't work here anymore. This really is as bad as I think it is,'" she says. "That red spoon has haunted me for a long time."

Before leaving, Ashley says she called Children and Youth Services for Berks County on Kate. In his book, Collin claimed a CYS investigation was triggered when he showed up to school in pain after Kate yanked his ear, and he said he later learned multiple reports were made against her.

"She did all the time," Ashley said of Kate's behavior towards Collin. "All the time. She'd rip him right out of his chair in the kitchen."

She says the reason she called CYS was because "I ended up getting sick because I started taking it home with me, because I didn't have my own kids and I didn't understand how somebody could be so nasty, downright evil and nasty to their own kids."

Ashley adds, "I know for a fact that I was not the only one who did that. I want to use this opportunity to not only back Collin that his mom was psychologically abusive to him, not to mention the physical."

By speaking out, Ashley, now a social worker, mental health advocate and mom to twins herself, hopes others will share their own experiences in the Gosselin family home.

"I really hope it will spark people to speak up, even if it's been 15 years later," she says. "I am so incredibly proud of Collin and hope he feels validated."

In 2024, Kate's attorney Richard Puleo told The Sun that he didn't believe that Kate had done anything to "intentionally harm" her son and that "she did what she did to protect herself and her family" from what he called "troubled behavior."

Addressing Collin's book on TikTok, Kate also liked a message from a user who claimed "he" would "regret all of this someday" and alleging that he'd been "encouraged and enabled by other dysfunctional and mentally ill people." They apologized for her having to "relive this over and over" and called the situation "gross."

"Exactly," Kate wrote in the same thread. "I had nothing to do with it, except for consent because it was medically necessary."

Kate and her attorney, Puleo, have not responded to requests for comment on Ashley and Collin's allegations. Children and Youth Services for Berks County declined to comment due to "strict confidentiality laws."

Collin's book In the Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood is out now wherever books are sold.

articles.title: Hila and Ethan Klein have made content together since 2011. Now she says he cheated for months.
articles.summary: Hila Klein, who started a YouTube channel with her husband in 2011 that now has 5.4 million subscribers, posted a lengthy statement on Instagram about the al...
articles.body:
Ethan Klein, a longtime YouTuber and H3 Podcast host, has been accused by his wife, Hila Klein, of having an affair.

Though the news is seemingly niche personal drama among content creators, outrage and schadenfreude have reverberated beyond their fan ecosystem, trending on Google Search and X .

In a lengthy statement posted on Instagram early Friday morning, Hila said she's separated from her husband, whom she's been with for nearly 20 years. Her post came hours after Ethan posted on his Instagram story that the H3 Podcast would be going on "indefinite hiatus."

"I am living a nightmare I can't wake up from. My husband has been having an affair. I have been fed lie after lie after lie for months. Here is the truth," she wrote.

Hila said she caught Ethan in a lie. "But the lies continued. 'It was just a kiss' became 'it was emotional cheating,'" she continued. "After I dragged these lies from him, he finally admitted he'd been in an affair for over 6 months, the extent of which I'm sure I still don't know."

Hila and Ethan are also business partners who have been collaborating as content creators since 2011, when they first launched a YouTube channel, H3H3 Productions . They started the H3 Podcast in 2016, and it currently has 5.4 million subscribers.

"The betrayal I feel is immeasurable. The person I loved and trusted for 20 years evaporated overnight. He was my safe place, my partner in marriage, parenting, and business," Hila said. "My only family on this side of the world. How do I even begin to make sense of this?"

The production crew of Ethan's H3 Podcast also issued a statement on Instagram , saying they "stand with Hila" and are "disgusted by Ethan's actions and the hurt he caused."

"We are all shocked, angry, and heartbroken to learn about Ethan's ongoing affair," the H3 team wrote. "As soon as we found out, we all agreed: we would not continue working with Ethan involved or profiting in any way. We don't yet know what that means for the future. There's a lot to work through, and we wish we had more answers for you."

Over the years, Ethan has built a considerable fan base — and earned a number of detractors — by positioning himself as both an arbiter and instigator of internet drama. The news has been hitting hard on both sides .

Yahoo has reached out to involved parties for comment.

articles.title: JK Rowling refuses to back down in essay calling trans activism 'elitist to its core'
articles.summary: Author J.K. Rowling's new essay defended her stance on women's single-sex spaces while calling modern transgender activism "elitist to its core."
articles.body: Author J.K. Rowling reaffirmed her stance on sex and gender issues Wednesday, writing in a new essay that she would not back down from her advocacy despite facing what she described as a relentless "avalanche of death, rape and torture threats." The British author, best known for writing the "Harry Potter" series, published the piece six years after her June 2020 essay sparked widespread debate over transgender rights and women's single-sex spaces. Rowling wrote that her views "haven’t changed" since 2020, but that "the landscape certainly has, and my own involvement in the issue has become practical as well as theoretical, so I thought it was time for an update." JK ROWLING CONFRONTS THE BBC FOR PUSHING 'PROPAGANDA' OVER ITS TRANSGENDER SPORTS HEADLINE Her original essay drew criticism from LGBTQ+ advocacy organizations and transgender rights activists, along with calls to boycott her work. In the new essay, Rowling defended her opposition to policies allowing transgender women into certain female-only spaces, arguing that they undermine protections for women. She also characterized modern transgender activism as "elitist to its core." "It’s true, of course, that trans activism doesn’t impact all women negatively. In fact, the more privileged you are, the less it tends to affect you, and the more it might benefit you. Aside from an avalanche of death, rape and torture threats, it hasn’t noticeably affected my life," Rowling wrote. Rowling has rejected accusations that her views are "anti-trans," maintaining that her advocacy centers on women's safety and privacy. "Should trans people be discriminated against when it comes to housing or employment? Of course not," Rowling wrote. "Should trans people be stripped of their human rights, or denied personal safety? Again: of course not." HBO’S 'HARRY POTTER' GETS A HARD NO FROM 'BLACK MIRROR,' 'LOKI' DIRECTORS OVER JK ROWLING’S TRANS VIEWS Earlier this month, transgender rights activists protested a gala performance of "Harry Potter and the Cursed Child" in London. A demonstrator wore a T-shirt reading, "Rowling money kills," and security personnel eventually removed the protesters from the red carpet. In response to Rowling’s earlier 2020 comments on sex and gender, LGBTQ+ advocacy group GLAAD criticized the author, writing on social media that "JK Rowling continues to align herself with an ideology which willfully distorts facts about gender identity and people who are trans. In 2020, there is no excuse for targeting trans people." Actor Daniel Radcliffe, who starred as Harry Potter in the film adaptations, also publicly criticized Rowling's comments in 2020, issuing a statement through The Trevor Project. "Transgender women are women," Radcliffe wrote. "Any statement to the contrary erases the identity and dignity of transgender people and goes against all advice given by professional health care associations who have far more expertise on this subject matter than either Jo or I." ROYAL FAMILY FACES BACKLASH FROM CRITICS AFTER QUEEN CAMILLA HOSTS JK ROWLING May Mailman, director of the Independent Women's Law Center, told Fox News Digital that she agrees with Rowling's criticism of wealthy supporters of transgender activism, arguing that working-class women are more likely to be affected by policies governing single-sex spaces. "For people in the United States who have real problems to deal with, they need to figure out how they're [going to] put food on the table," Mailman said. "They're not worried about pronouns. They're worried about improving their families and improving themselves. And so, there is this elitism that's like when you run out of problems, you start inventing them." Rowling has also supported the campaign group For Women Scotland, which challenged the interpretation of "woman" under the U.K.'s Equality Act 2010. On April 16, 2025, the U.K. Supreme Court ruled that the terms "woman" and "sex" refer to biological sex for the purposes of the law. The court also affirmed that transgender people remain protected against discrimination under the law's gender reassignment provisions. Mailman welcomed the British court decision but warned that she believes free speech in the country is increasingly under threat. "I think the status of free speech in Great Britain is much more under attack than it is in the U.S.," Mailman said, adding, "I think we should treat it as a warning sign, because I think people look to Britain as where the United States could and often does head." JK ROWLING CALLS OUT THE 'GROTESQUE' BEHAVIOR TOWARDS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FANS IN SCATHING POST Jeremiah Igunnubole, U.K. legal counsel for Alliance Defending Freedom International, a Christian legal advocacy group, also welcomed Rowling’s essay in a statement to Fox News Digital. "We welcome JK Rowling doubling down on her determination to challenge gender ideology and defend the importance of biological reality. Truth matters, and we should not be afraid to uphold it simply because doing so is controversial," Igunnubole said. He added that Alliance Defending Freedom International would "continue to defend these principles and the protections that flow from them robustly, including through litigation in the UK where necessary." articles.title: "We're just a step behind" - what McLaren is trying to solve with its final 2026 upgrades
articles.summary: Slow-corner performance remains a problem for the "knife edge" MCL40, so McLaren has been working towards a revised suspension geometry as well as a differen...
articles.body:
"To get the car to be quick, we just have to try so hard to be perfect, and you cannot be perfect," said Lando Norris after practice for the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix in Austin.

Two mid-season wins for Norris now appear to be a 'purple patch' rather than harbingers of a competitive renaissance for McLaren after a troubled start to the 2026 season. At the US GP it introduced the first elements of what will be the final upgrade package of the year, due to be introduced in stages between this event and the Las Vegas GP.

Although by mid-season McLaren had developed the MCL40 to the point where it was among the fastest cars through quick corners, straightline speed and slow-corner performance have continued to be problematic, as has its nervous demeanour. Development has had to balance the process not just of creating theoretical performance, but also of making the car benign enough for the drivers to tap into that potential.

"It's just on a knife edge on every single corner," said the reigning world champion in Singapore. "You've just got to drive it within an exact percent, and you have to force the car in every single way. You can't let the car do any work. You can't just let the front do the work, or the rear do the work. You have to force the front; you've got to force the rear.

"You've got to drive it in a way that takes so much concentration and so much ability. It's just full-on and mentally draining because of how hard you have to work behind the wheels.

"It's just too difficult and it makes it impossible to put laps together in qualifying, which just shows how good of a job we were able to do when we were getting on pole [in Hungary, the Netherlands and Spain], and how rewarding that felt."

Slow-corner performance isn't just a function of aerodynamics. Although Norris has a more adaptable style than many other drivers, even this requires the car to have a certain set of virtues. He takes a shallower approach to the apex than others, overlapping throttle and brake to a higher degree. His strength is a tremendous feel for where the front tyres pick up lateral grip mid-corner, which he exploits to help rotate the car.

What operates against him is the trend towards running a high degree of anti-squat, anti-dive geometry in the suspension. Although this stabilises the car's aerodynamic platform, it smothers the transmission of 'feel' about the changing state of grip at each axle. Shorn of this, Norris can't trust either end of the car – which is why, last year, his performances picked up dramatically after a slow start when McLaren developed an alternate front suspension geometry suspension for him.

In that context it's no surprise that McLaren has led with a revised front-end geometry for this latest update in Austin, along with reprofiled diffuser furniture. It's understood that the next phase of the upgrade will be applied in Brazil, with more arriving for Las Vegas depending on manufacturing timescales.

The new components McLaren will bring to the car in the coming races were signed off between the Dutch GP in late August and the Italian GP in the first week of September, and have been making their way through the production process. McLaren's design resources have been fully focused on the 2027 car ever since.

Insiders say the team identified a new aerodynamic direction during the April interregnum caused by the cancellation of the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian grands prix. The belief was that it would ultimately lead to a higher performance ceiling than the concept with which the team started the season.

This is a relatively typical occurrence in F1, especially during a new rules cycle. But it is very easy to leap to the conclusion that an upgrade package has somehow been a failure if it doesn't deliver an immediate and significant lap time uplift. From an engineering point of view it is simply establishing a new baseline.

McLaren introduced the first iteration of its new aerodynamic concept in the Azerbaijan GP weekend, centring around a dramatically different sidepod profile, along with heavily revised geometries for the flow conditioners in and around the diffuser, the leading edge of the floor, and the rear suspension fairings. The team was careful to manage expectations, emphasising that it wasn't expecting a major improvement in lap time straight away.

Circumstances then combined to make the new configuration appear, superficially, to be ineffective: Norris was stymied by a fuel injection problem while Oscar Piastri laboured to keep the Red Bulls of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar behind him in the early phase of the race, then dropped out of the points after locking up at the second safety car restart. Later the team admitted that at least some of the straightline speed deficit was a consequence of not getting the most out of its Mercedes power unit.

"We will be having some more upgrades coming for the final part of the season, which is the kind of upgrades that follow the foundation set with the upgrades we delivered in Baku," said team principal Andrea Stella after the Singapore round.

"The step in Baku wasn't expected to be big, but it was foundational for some stuff that we will start taking trackside as of Austin and for the coming races. So what's most important for me is that I look forward to seeing our competitiveness from the next race. And hopefully we will be back to being in condition to score podiums and hopefully, once the full package is delivered, to compete for the victory."

McLaren isn't the only team to find itself combatting instability as it tries to add performance to its car. Mercedes went to the extent of running two different car specs in Singapore to try to understand the behaviour of its latest upgrade – but, notably, it has opted for the latest spec in Austin. As Norris explained ahead of the US GP weekend, upgrading an F1 car isn't a predictable and linear process.

"Upgrades are not always just you put them on and things work," he said. "They're not always easy to get the full potential out of. I think we've had a car which has just been still so, so difficult to drive. Yes, we won two races and I had a couple of podium positions, but it was by tiny margins. With a car like that, you'll not be able to do that consistently.

"We need to also improve the car in terms of ease of driving and ease of extracting performance."

articles.body:
Oswaldo Montenegro canta 'Valsinha' (1971) e 'A noite do meu bem' (1959) no álbum 'Serenata' entre regravações de músicas do repertório do artista — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Aos 70 anos, Oswaldo Montenegro tem mantido a média de um álbum por ano. Transitando entre releituras da própria obra e eventuais apresentações de músicas inéditas, o cantor e compositor segue em contínua atividade nos palcos e nos estúdios.

“Serenata” – álbum lançado pelo artista ontem, sexta-feira, 23 de outubro – é um disco de voz e piano em que Montenegro revisita o cancioneiro autoral entre incursões pelos repertórios de Chico Buarque – de quem regrava “Valsinha” (1971), parceria de Chico com Vinicius de Moraes (1913 – 1980) – e Dolores Duran (1930 – 1959), compositora da qual o artista dá voz à obra-prima “A noite do meu bem” (1959). O cantor se acompanha ao piano em clima intimista.

Antecedido pelo single “Como se estivesse fora”, lançado em 16 de outubro com a gravação dessa parceria de Montenegro com Mongol (1957 – 2021) apresentada originalmente em 1980, o álbum “Serenata” tem repertório dominado por canções da extensa discografia do artista. “Lua e flor” (1984) é a mmais conhecida ao lado de “Agonia” (Mongol, 1980).

Músicas como “A voz da tela” (Oswaldo Montenegro e Márcio Guimarães, 1995), “Estrela de neon” (Mongol, 1992), “Luzes acesas” (2023) – bissexta e recente parceria de Montenegro com Raimundo Fagner – e “Rasura” (1999) também figuram entre as 15 faixas do álbum “Serenata”.

articles.standfirst: Roteiro de “Amoitado” foi inspirado em experiência real do diretor Tero Queiroz; curta de "suspense rural" será exibido pela primeira vez ao público no dia 30 de outubro.
articles.summary: Roteiro de “Amoitado” foi inspirado em experiência real do diretor Tero Queiroz; curta de "suspense rural" será exibido pela primeira vez ao público no dia 30 de outubro.
articles.body:
Imagens durante as garvações de Amoitado. — Foto: Divulgação

Uma experiência real com o roubo de gado, crime conhecido como abigeato, inspira um suspense rural no curta-metragem Amoitado, que está prestes a estrear em Campo Grande. O filme nasceu de uma memória de infância do diretor e roteirista Tero Queiroz.

Dirigido por Tero Queiroz, com codireção de Aly Freitas, Amoitado integra a Mostra Competitiva Curta MS e será exibido na próxima sexta-feira (30), às 20h, na Estação Cultural Teatro do Mundo.

Com 25 minutos de duração, o filme mistura suspense e ficção para contar uma história inspirada em uma lembrança da infância de Tero. A produção foi gravada em Campo Grande, principalmente à noite, e conta com 15 atores sul-mato-grossenses.

Tero cresceu em fazendas nos arredores de Rochedo e Corguinho, onde acompanhava o pai no trabalho rural. Quando tinha entre 8 e 10 anos, os dois encontraram um grupo roubando gado em uma propriedade vizinha. Para não serem vistos, precisaram se esconder e esperar os criminosos irem embora.

O episódio ficou na memória do diretor e, anos depois, virou inspiração para o roteiro.

“Um dia eu estava sentado aqui e falei, vou escrever alguma coisa sobre isso. E daí nasce o Amoitado”, contou Tero.

Na história real, o grupo roubou uma ou duas vacas. Para o filme, o diretor ampliou a situação com elementos de ficção.

“Uma história que era sucinta de um grupo pequeno roubando gado. E eu coloco um grupo estruturado, com uma família por trás, uma família que trabalha com empreendimento de roubo de gado”, explicou.

'Amoitado' é um curta-metragem de suspense que retrata o roubo de gados em MS. — Foto: Divulgação

As filmagens ocorreram na última semana de janeiro de 2026, em quatro locações de Campo Grande. A maior parte das cenas foi gravada à noite, para acompanhar o contexto do roubo de gado retratado na história.

A produção incluiu perseguições, tiroteios e cenas com chuva artificial. Segundo Tero, foram cinco dias de gravação noturna. O diretor também destacou que queria trabalhar com um elenco maior do que o habitual em curtas-metragens.

A exibição no Festival Curta Campo Grande marca a primeira vez que Amoitado será apresentado ao público. Tero explicou que a equipe pretende inscrever o filme em outros festivais brasileiros e internacionais.

“Por hora, as janelas que a gente está interessado e vai levar esse filme são os festivais”, afirmou o diretor.

Segundo ele, esses eventos são os principais espaços de circulação para curtas-metragens.

O Festival Curta Campo Grande chega à terceira edição em 2026 e reúne 61 filmes brasileiros e estrangeiros. As produções estão distribuídas em quatro mostras competitivas: Curta MS, Curta Brasil, Curta Doc e Panorama Internacional.

O evento ocorre entre os dias 26 e 31 de outubro, com sessões em espaços culturais e escolas da capital. A programação também inclui debates, palestra, aula magna, encontro de realizadores e cerimônia de premiação.

articles.title: Julie Andrews Seen in Public for First Time Since Announcing She’s Almost “Completely Retired”
articles.summary: The Oscar winner turned 91 earlier this month.
articles.body:
Julie Andrews was spotted in the Hamptons, New York on October 16.

The actress turned 91 earlier this month.

In August, Andrews revealed that she's almost "completely retired."

Julie Andrews enjoyed a rare outing two months after revealing that she's almost "completely retired." The actress , 91, was photographed in the Hamptons , New York on October 16.

In photos obtained by Page Six , Andrews could be seen wearing a purple coat, a white baseball cap, and sunglasses as got out of her car.

Andrews, who turned 91 on October 1, last walked a red carpet in 2023. More recently, she revealed her decision to step away from onscreen roles. Speaking with The Hollywood Reporter in August, Andrews explained why she decided not to return for the third installment in the Princess Diaries film franchise.

"I think the absolute truth is that I think I'm really past all that now," she told the magazine. "I'm not completely retired, but it's a different kind of work that I do these days—[writing] books, and I do a lot of recording of podcasts and voiceovers. But truly, I don't think I should be a part of it."

Andrews added that it's "still lovely to be working on things," though not "necessarily on camera."

"It isn't that I'm not enthusiastic for it. It's just that I really don't feel I should be part of it now," she continued.

Based on Meg Cabot's books of the same name, the original Princess Diaries movie came out in 2001. Anne Hathaway is set to reprise her role as Mia Thermopolis in the upcoming third installment. In the same THR interview, Andrews was asked about what she thinks the new film will entail.

"Actually don't know," she said. "I think it proceeds from the second Princess Diaries . It moves on, but by now Annie too is a little older than she was when she did it. I'm interested to see what Meg [Cabot] and Annie and everybody comes up with."

articles.title: Celebs on Vidyarambham:A day to honour gurus and embrace learning
articles.summary: Vidyarambham on Vijayadasami is significant for artists and anyone pursuing a form of learning.
articles.body: Vidyarambham on Vijayadasami is significant for artists and anyone pursuing a form of learning. While it marks the beginning of formal education for some, for others, it is an opportunity to start afresh and hone their craft. Celebrities share how they marked the special day.I started with the initiation of new students: Vineeth Actor-dancer Vineeth turned teacher a while ago, and his Vidyarambham begins with initiating new students at his dance school, followed by pujas rooted in his guru’s traditions.“Every year, we have a ritualistic celebration with chilanka puja and Saraswathi puja. After that, we wear the bells and perform guru parampara vandanam, a tradition I learnt from my guru, Sree Padma Subrahmanyam. I follow her pedagogy and the way she conducts the Vijayadashami rituals. We begin with basic adavus and wrap up the celebrations with performances by senior students.“When you start teaching, you realise the value of teaching. You become a student again! I am enjoying that phase now,” he says.My fans did something special for women auto drivers: AnumolActress Anumol celebrated Vijayadashami in a unique way with the support of her fans. She began the day by calling her gurus and seeking their blessings. However, a special initiative by her fan group made the occasion even more meaningful.“A group of fans called Anumol Fangirls, who are like family to me, sponsored auto pujas for 50 women auto drivers in Chennai. They also provided first-aid kits, water bottles, bags, power banks and six months’ worth of sanitary pads. I took part in the initiative to support them and thank them. On a day when we begin learning, doing something like this for women, by women, is heartening,” she says.Anumol makes it a point to meet her teachers wherever she is, depending on who lives nearby. “There are teachers who taught me different things. Whichever city I am in, I try to meet those who are closer to the place,” she says.She also begins the day by writing Om Hari Shree Ganapathaye Namah. “Unlike in our childhood, I now read texts on my phone. Those days when we would accidentally read something on TV and run to our mothers to ask if it was okay to do so during puja are long gone! I have also had the fortune of initiating Vidyarambham for children,” she adds.Every Vidyarambham, I become a student: Rachana NarayanankuttyActress-dancer Rachana Narayanankutty marked the day by introducing her students to a new subject — a global perspective on the Natyasastra.“It is about connecting the Natyasastra with global art forms, and it has a philosophical aspect. Our classes began with that. I had dance sessions for all my students, both online and in person. I still have more classes to take in the afternoon. Later, I will visit my teachers, Thrissur Janardhanan Mash and Gita Padmakumari Teacher, and offer them dakshina,” she says.Her day will not end until she finishes classes with her students based in the US and Canada.For Rachana, Vidyarambham is as much about learning as it is about teaching. “Every Vidyarambham, I become a student. The quality we need as artists is the willingness to remain a student. We can learn a lot from each of our students, and I eagerly look forward to discovering what I can learn from them. Every student is an individual, and each has a different approach to art. There is so much to learn from them,” she says.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: I never choose a film thinking, 'This will work with families': Nivin Pauly
articles.summary: With Bethlehem Kudumba Unit (BKU) becoming Malayalam cinema’s biggest blockbuster in terms of footfalls, its success has reinforced something audiences
articles.body: With Bethlehem Kudumba Unit (BKU) becoming Malayalam cinema’s biggest blockbuster in terms of footfalls, its success has reinforced something audiences have come to appreciate about Nivin Pauly: his ability to inhabit characters that feel real. From the repeat-viewing appeal of family dramas to experimenting with different genres, the actor reflects on career choices, the evolving Malayalam film market, social media and the speculation of a reunion with Dulquer Salmaan. Excerpts:What does BKU becoming Malayalam cinema’s biggest blockbuster by footfalls mean to you personally?What has been especially beautiful about BKU is the repeat viewing. Someone watches it with friends and returns with their family. Young people are bringing their parents and grandparents. Milestones like this are wonderful, but they will eventually be surpassed. Malayalam cinema is seeing industry hits more frequently, which is a healthy sign. It means the audience is growing, the market is expanding and bigger achievements are possible. I’m sure the next industry hit is already on its way. For me, the real happiness is that BKU became part of that growth.Age-gap romances can be tricky, as even a small misstep can affect how a relationship is perceived. Did you have any reservations about playing Justin?Every relationship needs to be handled with sensitivity, and this one was no different. What I appreciate about Justin is that he never tries to control Ashley or treats love as ownership. Even when things get difficult, he doesn’t try to separate her from her parents or force her to choose between them and him. They aren’t perfect people, and theirs isn’t a perfect relationship. But there is respect, freedom and a genuine choice to be together. That is what makes their relationship beautiful.Is family-oriented cinema a space where you naturally shine, or have the right films, such as Sarvam Maya and BKU, found you?Family audiences are the hardest to connect with, because you’re not speaking to one age group or one kind of viewer. A teenager, a parent and a grandparent can watch the same film for completely different reasons. So when a film connects across generations, I don’t see a 'family-film space'; I see emotions universal enough to travel. I’ve always been drawn to characters who feel close to life: flawed, funny, vulnerable, sometimes confused. Maybe audiences find it easy to place me in those worlds. But I never choose a film thinking, 'This will work with families'. I choose it because I believe in the character and the emotional truth of the story. With BKU, Girish created a family that doesn’t feel designed for cinema. They’re messy, affectionate, irritating and real. That excited me.You’ve experimented with different kinds of films, some with mixed results. Has that ever made you hesitant?Instinct has guided me throughout my career, starting with my decision to quit my IT job and pursue cinema. Some of my experiments worked, others didn’t, but both gave me clarity. Failure can make you cautious, but if it makes you afraid, you stop growing as an actor. The lesson was never to stop experimenting, but to understand myself better. Now, the question is how much of what people love about me I can retain while still surprising them.Was there a particular experience or decision in the last few years that changed how you look at your career today?Success tells you what works, while failure forces you to understand your choices, mistakes and strengths. Both are necessary. The most important thing is not to give up during a difficult phase. In cinema, one Friday can change everything. But you can’t simply wait for that Friday to arrive. You have to keep working, preparing and improving so you’re ready when it does.You’ve always had an easy connection with humour and everyday characters. Has comedy become more instinctive with experience?A lot of the best humour comes from behaviour... a hesitation, a reaction, an awkward silence or just the way one person looks at another. I really enjoy that kind of comedy, and I genuinely enjoy the process of shooting those scenes. I usually feel very relaxed going into a comedy sequence. A big part of that also comes from my co-actors. Sometimes I enjoy their performances so much that I find it difficult to stop laughing during a take. So, yes, maybe comedy has become more instinctive with experience, but for me, the most important thing is still enjoying the moment and reacting honestly to the people around me.Does making people laugh require a different approach in a family entertainer, or is comedy better when you don’t consciously try to be funny?I prefer not trying too hard to be funny. If the character knows he is delivering a joke, sometimes the humour disappears. But if the character is completely serious and the situation becomes funny for the audience, that is much more enjoyable for me. In a family entertainer especially, humour has to travel across generations. A teenager, a parent and a grandparent may laugh at completely different things in the same scene. So, rather than designing every moment as a punchline, I think it is better to make the situation truthful. Humour usually finds its own way out of that.How do you build chemistry with your co-stars? Your on-screen partnership with Aju Varghese seems to have that chemistry, too...We don’t have to try to create chemistry or build a bond with our co-stars. It happens naturally. We just need to be ourselves. With Aju, it is nice because we are such close friends, and we are close even as families. Even if we don’t have a lot of friends, having a few good friends is still great.Your Tamil projects are at very different ends of the spectrum — an arthouse film like Yezhu Kadal Yezhu Malai and a mass entertainer like Benz. Is that contrast something you consciously look for outside Malayalam cinema?With Ram sir and Yezhu Kadal Yezhu Malai, I entered a completely different cinematic world. The rhythm, philosophy and approach to a character were very different from those in the films I normally do. Benz gives me a completely different kind of energy and scale. I didn’t want to approach the character thinking, ‘Now I have to behave like a villain.’ That can become very external. The more interesting question for me was: why does this man believe he is justified in what he is doing? Most people don’t wake up thinking they are the villain in somebody else’s story. They have their own logic, ego, wounds and ambitions. Finding that internal logic was much more interesting to me than simply trying to look threatening. I enjoy that contrast.How active are you on social media? Do you follow conversations about your films and performances, and do they affect you?Social media is a great way to gauge how people respond to your work. Audiences show their love through messages, edits and posts, and also offer constructive criticism. But it’s not healthy to form an opinion based entirely on social media. Algorithms can keep showing us a particular pattern that may not reflect the wider audience. Personal messages can be more useful because when someone takes the time to explain what moved them or didn’t work, you get a more honest sense of how your work is reaching people.Some Malayalam actors have built a presence across multiple Indian film industries. Do you have similar pan-India ambitions?I’m definitely open to working in different languages. Today, good films can travel far beyond the language in which they are made. For me, what matters most is finding the right character, filmmaker and story.With the OTT boom expanding Malayalam cinema’s reach, do you think the talk of a bigger market is justified?It’s something to be proud of when people speak well of Malayalam cinema. More writers and directors can help us grow further, both in content and commercial success. We also need big films that gross ₹700 crore or ₹1,000 crore, but they must be content-driven. That’s what audiences expect, too. Earlier, even ₹100 crore was a rare milestone. We’ve come a long way, with films grossing ₹300 crore in the last two Onam seasons. Now, the industry is also more connected with distributors outside Kerala. Not every film will work in every region, so we need to understand its core audience and position it accordingly. If a film has potential in a particular market, we should be ready to push it. We did that with BKU and Sarvam Maya. Manjummel Boys, Aavesham and Premalu have also travelled well. It needs strategic planning and a team ready to act when an opportunity arises.We hear your name connected to several projects. What do you have lined up?Dear Students is awaiting release. Multiverse Manmadhan is in the rewriting phase. The same goes for the film with Alphonse Puthren (Premam). Everyone is taking their time to make the scripts better, so I agreed that we should take our time and make decisions as we go. I also have a project with Nashid Famy, the writer of Jaya Jaya Jaya Jaya Hey. It is a fun entertainer, and that is progressing in parallel. I haven’t decided what I will do next after that.On reuniting with Dulquer Salmaan...In Bangalore Days, Dulquer and I played cousins. When we met at an award function after a long gap, his warmth immediately brought back that cousin-like bond. Later, Dulquer distributed my film with Ram sir, Yezhu Kadal Yezhu Malai, in Kerala, and people began speculating about a reunion. We’d both be excited to work together again; it’s about finding the right project. Given the affection and expectations surrounding our reunion, we’d want the film to live up to that excitement.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Irrfan Khan knew his days were numbered’: Abhinay Deo on his final talk with the actor
articles.summary: Filmmaker Abhinay Deo recently looked back on his time with Irrfan Khan during the making of the dark comedy 'Blackmail' (2018), praising the late actor’s
articles.body: Filmmaker Abhinay Deo recently looked back on his time with Irrfan Khan during the making of the dark comedy 'Blackmail' (2018), praising the late actor’s dedication to his work. He recalled one scene in particular that has stayed with him. Though Irrfan was unwell, he ran nearly 200 metres in a single, uninterrupted take for a physically demanding shot. What touches Abhinay most is that he had no idea about Irrfan’s health at the time. He also spoke about their discussions around a possible sequel to the film, and how Irrfan responded when Abhinay promised they would collaborate again once his treatment was over.Irrfan Khan and the ‘Blackmail’ sequel that never happenedAs 'Blackmail' was nearing the end of its shoot, Abhinay, feeling sure of the film, had already begun talking to Irrfan about a sequel. The actor was equally keen on revisiting the story. By the time Irrfan saw the rough cut, his health had worsened, and Deo, now aware of his condition, met him to talk about working together again. “During the end of the shoot, I actually started discussing the part two with him because I was confident of this film. He was very excited and when he saw the film’s rough cut, by then we all knew that his health has taken a south turn. That time, I spoke to him and said, ‘See, Irrfan, wherever you are going, Germany or wherever, just go, get well and return soon, we have to do the second part.’ So, he started laughing and said, ‘Yeah, yeah, we’ll do.’ But, somewhere, he knew that his days were numbered.”Abhinay Deo on Irrfan Khan’s dedication to his craftIn a conversation with SCREEN, Abhinay revealed that he made a habit of noticing the small details in Irrfan’s acting, and they never failed to leave an impression on him. Talking about the late actor, the director said, “There are so many things about him. He was an extremely spontaneous actor, one of the finest our country has ever had. He used to study his characters extensively, but you could never tell that he had done so much preparation. You never got the feeling that he was performing something he had rehearsed. His performances flowed like water. He was so spontaneous, and it was fabulous to watch him.”When Irrfan Khan ran 200 metres in one takeLooking back on the moment, Deo shared, “There was a scene in Blackmail where I needed him to run for almost 200 metres without stopping, in a single shot. At the end of those 200 metres, he had to stop and emote, showing the turmoil of a man who had just seen his wife with someone else. He simply ran because there was no other way to do the scene. And, I didn’t know at that point in time that he was not well.”“I told him, ‘See, Irrfan, if we manage in this shot then great, otherwise, we will have to retake the scene.’ He said, ‘Yes, we’ll do.’ He still didn’t tell me that he isn’t well. He did once, did the second time, and in the third attempt, I said, ‘Let’s do one last take for tighter frames.’ And, Irrfan said, ‘Abhinay, this is the last take because after this, I might fall.’ I got shocked, and thought maybe he is tired because it was in the middle of the night,” said the director.How Abhinay Deo learned about Irrfan Khan’s diagnosisAbhinay shared that it was only a few days after the shoot that he learned Irrfan had been diagnosed with cancer. Reflecting on it, he said, “A few days later, I got to know that he is…this was the commitment level; that guy just ran and ran in that state. These memories are truly special because they remind me of a great man at work, someone who was completely dedicated to his craft.”Irrfan Khan’s death at 53Irrfan passed away on April 29, 2020, at 53, after fighting a neuroendocrine tumour. articles.title: Neil Nitin Mukesh reacts to Tiger Shroff firing incident; calls it an ‘eye-opener’ as police recover weapons in Surat
articles.summary: Actor Neil Nitin Mukesh has reacted to the shooting incident involving Tiger Shroff, describing it as frightening and an opportunity to reflect on the
articles.body: Actor Neil Nitin Mukesh has reacted to the shooting incident involving Tiger Shroff, describing it as frightening and an opportunity to reflect on the importance of humility. Tiger escaped relatively unharmed after unidentified assailants allegedly fired at his car in Mumbai's Juhu area on October 18. The incident has raised concerns about celebrity security, while Mumbai Police continue investigating the attack.Speaking to Mid-Day, Neil Nitin Mukesh expressed disbelief over the incident and spoke about his longstanding relationship with Tiger Shroff's family. He shares a close bond with Jackie Shroff, whom he affectionately calls Jaggu Da. Their families have known each other for generations, and Neil has worked with Jackie in two films.Neil Nitin Mukesh calls incident an ‘eye-opener’The actor, known for his performance in 'Johnny Gaddaar', said the shooting should encourage people to remain humble and grounded. He also suggested that public figures should be mindful of their behaviour and avoid unnecessary attention."It's scary, and at the same time, it's an eye-opener. It reminds us to be humble, grounded and a little quiet at times."Neil Nitin Mukesh further explained that incidents like this can affect how actors interact with people. While celebrities may become cautious about their safety, they can also face criticism for avoiding public interactions." Episodes like this bring a bit of fear and insecurity to everyone. Because if actors are rushing out and don't want to interact, they are judged for that, too. So, it's a two-way street," Neil mentioned.Neil Nitin Mukesh expresses concern for Tiger ShroffNeil Nitin Mukesh described Tiger Shroff as a well-brought-up person and questioned why anyone would target him. The actor also recalled his family's longstanding association with Jackie Shroff, who has been a father figure to them."It's very sad. He is such a nice boy. I know his family so well. Jaggu da is like a father figure to us. We have known each other for generations. He knows my father and my grandfather. I had the opportunity to work with him and have done two films with Jaggu da. I know Tiger, too. He is such a nice, well-brought-up boy. Why? Why would this happen?"Mumbai police recover two firearms in SuratMeanwhile, the Mumbai Crime Branch has recovered two firearms allegedly used in the attack, along with 10 live cartridges, from Surat in Gujarat, PTI reported. The recovery was made on Friday during targeted raids connected to the investigation.Police officials said investigators traced the weapons' supply route to a hideout in Surat. The recovered firearms and ammunition have been sent for forensic examination and ballistic testing. Investigators will compare the findings with empty shell casings collected from the crime scene.The attack took place in Juhu on the evening of October 18. At least two men allegedly fired at Tiger Shroff's car before escaping on a motorcycle. The actor escaped relatively unhurt, while his driver and a bystander sustained injuries.Mumbai Police said five to six rounds were fired. A motorcycle suspected to have been used by the assailants was later found abandoned in Andheri. A case has been registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Arms Act for attempted murder and other offences. Ten people have been apprehended so far, with arrests reported in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Haryana.Reports say that the Mumbai Police have named gangster Anil Pandit as a wanted accused in the case. Pandit allegedly claimed responsibility for the October 18 attack in a social media post. He is also described as an associate of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, which is believed to be operating from the United States.The investigation remains underway as police examine the recovered weapons and pursue further leads.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'I'm not Alia Bhatt or Deepika Padukone': Radhika Apte explains why actresses are pushed into male-led films
articles.summary: Radhika Apte has spoken about the challenges faced by women-led films in Hindi cinema.
articles.body: Radhika Apte has spoken about the challenges faced by women-led films in Hindi cinema. She said that the actresses are almost forced to pick male-led projects for theatrical releases because of the uncertainty around box office. The actor, who is currently promoting her series ‘Akka’, believes only top stars like Alia Bhatt or Deepika Padukone can hope to bring audiences to cinemas on their own strength.Radhika Apte on female-led filmsRadhika Apte’s last few films, ‘Lust Stories 3’, ‘Saali Mohabbat’, ‘Mrs Undercover’ and ‘Monica, O My Darling’, all premiered directly on streaming platforms. However, she said that the medium never decides which films she says yes to."I don’t take a project based on whether it’s theatrical or OTT. I don’t really care about it. There are so many business decisions dependent on that; I’d rather be like, 'Let the film come out one way or another'," the actor told PTI in an interview.Radhika then explained why many women in the industry end up in films led by men. She said nobody has been able to tell what works in theatres in recent years.“With theatrical releases in the last few years, we don’t know what is working or what isn’t. A theatrical release where I am the lead would probably tank even if it’s the best film. I don’t have that, like, generally. I’m not an Alia Bhatt or Deepika Padukone where you can, at least, hope that they’ll be opening. I’m being very honest with you. That means I have to be in a film where men are doing the main part,” Radhika Apte said.What’s next for Radhika ApteRadhika Apte is now gearing up for the release of ‘Akka’, a gangster drama set in the 1980s. The series also stars Keerthy Suresh in the lead and will premiere on Netflix on October 30.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ranbir Kapoor’s ‘Ramayana’ sequel likely to miss Diwali 2027 release; makers need more shooting time for war sequences - Report
articles.summary: The second part of Nitesh Tiwari’s ‘Ramayana’ may not hit theatres during Diwali 2027 as planned.
articles.body: The second part of Nitesh Tiwari’s ‘Ramayana’ may not hit theatres during Diwali 2027 as planned. A report says producer Namit Malhotra is thinking of moving the sequel to Diwali 2028, so the team gets more time for filming and production. The makers have not yet shared a new date.Why the sequel may be delayedThe two films were first planned to release about a year apart. A shift to 2028 would widen that gap. As per a Bollywood Hungama report, the talks are linked to the extra shooting still pending for the second part. Its big war sequences are also said to be a reason behind the proposed change.According to the report, “Ramayana is an emotion for Namit Malhotra, and he is leaving no stone unturned to present the Indian audience with a cinema-watching experience like never before.”The report added, “While the first part is set to release in a couple of days from now, the second instalment needs some more shooting time.”Talking about the size of the film, the report further stated, “As everyone knows, the real scale of Ramayana is in the second part, where the war actually unfolds.”If the new schedule is locked, the team will get more room to finish the large action scenes in the final chapter. For now, the delay is only a report, and the production house has not made any official statement.First part arrives in November 2026‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’ is the first film in the two-part retelling of Valmiki’s ancient epic. It will release on November 5 in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam. Namit Malhotra is the producer, with Yash also on board as a producer. Prime Focus Studios is co-producing it with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations.Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, while Sai Pallavi appears as Goddess Sita. The beloved star was 93 years old at the time of his demise and was well known for his roles in ‘Top Gun,' 'Aliens,' ‘Picket Fences,' ‘War Hunt,' ‘Up In Smoke,' ‘The Turning Point,' and many others. Over the years, the actor had gathered quite a lot of wisdom from his experience in the industry, which also included lessons on how to live life and manage regret. He added, “I am healthy and reasonably sane." Skerritt also shared, "I've lived through everything, so what regrets could I have? I'm healthy and reasonably sane.
